problem: "Hydraulic power steering always drives a pump from the engine belt" is too absolute. Electro-hydraulic power steering (EHPS) exists on many cars: it keeps the hydraulic rack but drives the pump with an electric motor, not the engine belt. The word "always" makes a student mark a true statement false.
fix: "Conventional hydraulic power steering usually drives a pump from the engine belt (some systems use an electric pump instead); the pump circulates oil even when the wheel is straight, so it costs fuel."

problem: The caption and the aria text say the reduction gear turns motor torque into "assist torque at the rack", but the formula and Section 1 define assist torque at the pinion. The node note under "Rack assist" also says "torque at pinion", so the figure contradicts itself and the text.
fix: Make the figure say the same thing as the formula: "the 10:1 reduction gear turns motor torque into assist torque at the pinion (rack input)", and keep the node note consistent with that.

problem: "How far the wheel is turned from straight ahead" is ambiguous: it can be read as the road wheel angle. The steering angle sensor measures the steering-wheel rotation (several turns lock to lock), which is then converted to road-wheel angle.
fix: "A separate steering angle sensor measures how far the steering wheel is rotated from the straight-ahead position, usually over several turns lock to lock."

problem: The trap says "students often divide by N when they should multiply", but the worked example itself divides 8 N·m by 10 to get motor torque. Without saying which direction is which, a student may think the example breaks the rule.
fix: "The reduction ratio multiplies motor torque: assist torque = N × motor torque. To go from assist torque to motor torque, divide by N; to go from motor torque to assist torque, multiply by N."
